Blood Bowl 3 is being replaced by Warhammer Blood Bowl: What will happen to everyone's unspent currency?
summary: Should you spend it now, or can you safely keep it in the bank?
body: What happened Blood Bowl 3, the latest videogame iteration of Games Workshop's tabletop game of literal fantasy football, has an in-game store where a currency called Warpstone can be spent on cosmetics and new teams. An upgraded version called Warhammer Blood Bowl, now published by Slitherine rather than previous publisher Focus Home Interactive, is currently in beta and will eventually replace Blood Bowl 3. Slitherine has said anyone who owns Blood Bowl 3 will get Warhammer Blood Bowl for free, and their account will transfer over. But the way new teams are unlocked will be changing. Will we carry over our unspent Warpstone, or should we blow it all now before Blood Bowl 3 is deprecated when Warhammer Blood Bowl comes out later this year? Players are confused . I reached out to clarify the situation, and a Slitherine representative answered my questions. Here's the most important part: "Players will use the same BB account on both games, so they will instantly get all cosmetics, warpstones and teams they bought in BB3, into WH BB". But while you don't need to spend your Warpstone out of fear any leftovers will be lost, if you've got enough to splash out on a team that might be w…

title: We tried to earn as much gold in WoW: Forever as we could in 2 hours—which involved a mugging, slander, and at least one crashout
body: If you want to make money in World of Warcraft, well… I cannot rightly say that we at PC Gamer are any good at it, based on the evidence given to us—but we are at least inventing new ways of money-making. And isn't invention the mother of necessity? Or was it the other way around? Who cares, we've got pockets to line. I wrangled two of my erstwhile co-workers, Fraser Brown and Joshua Wolens, to see which of us was the best at making money in World of Warcraft: Forever's beta. Which felt like a fair testing ground, given both how populated it is and how un-inflated its new, fledgling economy would be. Here were the rules: We started as level 1 horde characters. We each had a nest-egg of 20 silver to get us started. Starting from our spawning points into Azeroth, we had to make as much gold as we could in two hours. There were some additional rules about auction house postings that didn't become relevant. No really. I spent a lot of time thinking about them and their implications for the challenge. None of us bothered. I'm definitely not mad about it. Each of us entered with a different strategy. Well, two of us did (more on that later) to try and make the most bank. I, the Orc of W…
